newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas eases on weather, ample storage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas eases on weather, ample storage.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices retreated Thursday as forecasts called for normal to above-normal temperatures across most of the U.S. next week, sources said.
Swing prices on the Gulf Coast pipes lost about five to 10 cents to the $2.91-2.96 per mmBtu range as mild temperatures left buyers relying on ample storage supplies in the East.
Early deals were reported done at Henry Hub, La., as high as $3.00.
Similarly in south Texas, prices fell by about 10 cents to the low-$2.80s due to the mild weather now in the region.

Despite cold weather now in parts of the Midwest and northern plains, prices on the Midcontinent pipes softened by about five cents to the $2.80-2.85 range. Late deals were reported done as low as $2.70.
Chicago city-gate values were talked equally lower in the $3.15-3.20 range.
In west Texas, Permian prices spiraled downward throughout this morning's trading. Traders said most deals were done in the $2.69-2.74 range, down more than 10 cents from Wednesday's range.
Prices at the southern California border also fell by about 10 cents to an average range of $2.79-2.84. Shortly before nomination deadlines, gas was selling around $2.75.
In the East, prices held fairly steady around $3.30 as cooler weather was forecast for the region Friday and then again on Sunday and Monday.
In the Appalachian region, prices on Columbia Gas ranged from about $3.05 early to $2.90 late. CNG values continued to carry a premium in the $3.10-3.20 range.
